newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia rubber down on weak regional sentiment.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia rubber down on weak regional sentiment.

text.p: Malaysian rubber prices ended the week lower, following an absence in consumer demand and a widespread fall in prices across the region.
"It's been falling all over -- Tokyo, Thailand, Indonesia and Singapore," said a trader.
"The U.S. buyers are on summer holidays while the others seem to have just disappeared.
At the close, the July RSS1 buyer price eased 1.50 cents to 276 cents ($1.10) a kg and July SMR 20 buyer dipped 3.50 cents to 253.50 cents.
A check with Malaysian trading houses at noon showed the SMR 20 offered at 251/252 cents, SMR 10 at 250/251, SMR 5 at 262/263, SMR CV at 321/322, SMR L at 300/301, and drum latex at 217/218.
The INRO five-day average was 208.62 Malaysian/Singapore cents per kg on June 19 from 209.81 on June 18. The daily indicator was at 205.37 against 207.30 previously.
A Malaysia-based shipping agent quoted freight rates for rubber from Malaysia to Rotterdam at $800 per TEU and $1,700 per two-TEU containers.
